Effects of management estimated from the project's own units

Source: R/effet_gestion.R
effet_gestion.Rd

Estimates, for each unit and each family index (or indicator), the effect of the declared management type compared with a reference type, from the units of the project themselves: a T- or X-learner (Kunzel et al. 2019) fitted on covariates that describe the site (P2, altitude, slope, SER). The overlap between treated and reference units is checked on a propensity score; units outside the common support are left out, and the function refuses to conclude when too few units are comparable (spec 068, chantier D, step 1). It needs no simulation model: it says what management has produced on this massif, so that a simulation can later be confronted with it.

Usage

effet_gestion(
  units,
  traitement = "type_sylviculture",
  resultats = NULL,
  covariables = c("P2", "altitude", "pente", "ser"),
  reference = NULL,
  methode = c("x_learner", "t_learner"),
  support_min = 0.7,
  min_par_traitement = 10L,
  n_boot = 50L,
  graine = 1L
)

Arguments

units

sf or data.frame of units.

traitement

Character. Column holding the declared management type (e.g. "type_sylviculture", or the itineraire_actuel of spec 065). Default "type_sylviculture".

resultats

Character. Outcome columns. NULL (default): the family indices present (famille_*).

covariables

Character. Site covariates. Only those present in units are used; at least one is required. Default c("P2", "altitude", "pente", "ser").

reference

Character. Reference level of traitement. NULL: the most frequent level.

methode

"x_learner" (default) or "t_learner".

support_min

Numeric in [0, 1]. Minimum share of the units of a contrast that must lie in the common support; below it the contrast is refused (recouvrement_insuffisant). Default 0.7 (spec 068, D-4).

min_par_traitement

Integer. Minimum number of units per level in a contrast; below it, trop_peu_unites. Default 10 (D-4).

n_boot

Integer. Bootstrap replicates for the intervals. Default 50.

graine

Integer. Random seed. Default 1.

Value

A list of class "effet_gestion":

resume

one row per contrast (traitement against reference) and outcome: traitement, reference, resultat, n_traite, n_reference, part_support, effet_moyen (doubly robust, AIPW, mean effect over the units in the support), ic_bas, ic_haut (90 % interval from its influence function), statut (calcule, recouvrement_insuffisant, trop_peu_unites).

unites

one row per unit of a computed contrast and outcome: unite (row number), traitement, resultat, effet (individual effect from the T- or X-learner), ic_bas, ic_haut (bootstrap 5-95 % quantiles, indicative), support; NA outside the support.

reference, methode, apprenant, covariables

what was used; apprenant is "ranger" when installed, else "lm".

Details

Learners. T-learner: one outcome model per group, the effect is the difference of their predictions. X-learner: the effects imputed in each group are modelled in turn and mixed by the propensity score, which suits unbalanced groups (Kunzel et al. 2019). Outcome models are random forests (ranger) when installed, else linear models.

Mean effect. The summary uses an augmented inverse-probability weighting estimator (AIPW, doubly robust) on the units in the support, with out-of-bag predictions of the outcome models; methode only changes the individual effects. On simulated data (150 units, effect 8, strong confounding by P2, 30 draws), the naive difference of means gave 18.5, the AIPW estimate 7.1 on average, and its 90 % interval covered the true value 93 % of the time: a small downward bias remains with forests.

Support. Propensity score by logistic regression on the covariates; a unit is in the common support when its score lies within the range shared by both groups and within [0.05, 0.95].

What it is not (fiche): an association adjusted for the covariates, not a causal effect unless every confounder is among them; a declared management type is not necessarily the one applied; with few units per type the intervals are wide. Results enter the AI perspectives as results of the project, cited as such.

Lifecycle

Experimental (spec 068): may change in any release.

References

Kunzel, S. R., Sekhon, J. S., Bickel, P. J. & Yu, B. (2019). Metalearners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects using machine learning. PNAS 116(10), 4156-4165.

See also

comparer_itineraires()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 120
d <- data.frame(P2 = runif(n, 2, 10), altitude = runif(n, 200, 900))
d$type_sylviculture <- ifelse(runif(n) < plogis((d$P2 - 6) / 2), "irregulier", "regulier")
d$famille_biodiversite <- 40 + 3 * d$P2 + 8 * (d$type_sylviculture == "irregulier") + rnorm(n, 0, 3)
e <- effet_gestion(d, reference = "regulier", n_boot = 20)
e$resume
#>   traitement reference             resultat n_traite n_reference part_support
#> 1 irregulier  regulier famille_biodiversite       68          52          0.8
#>   effet_moyen   ic_bas  ic_haut  statut
#> 1    7.928485 6.329075 9.527895 calcule
